class.name: NetDriver
class.brief_description: Connections, travel, and the mirroring of everything the server creates.
class.description: It sits at [code]/root/NetDriver[/code] on every peer and is never freed with a level, which is what lets it be the address remote calls are sent to: a call only arrives if the node holding it is at the same path on both sides. Spawning goes through here rather than through a [MultiplayerSpawner] because a client is only sent what it can receive: a peer counts as ready once it has reported the current level up, and until then nothing is sent to it. That is also what makes a late join and a level change the same case - the peer is handed the whole world once, in one place. Projects rarely call it directly; [method World.server_travel] and the game mode's login path drive it. [method is_peer_ready] is the useful one, and it is what the framework's synchronizers filter their visibility on.

method.name: client_create_player_controller
method.description: Remote call: build this client's own controller. A client holds no other player's controller.

method.name: client_despawn_pawn
method.description: Remote call: a pawn is gone.

method.name: client_despawn_player_state
method.description: Remote call: a player left; drop their player state.

method.name: client_destroy_player_controller
method.description: Remote call: this client's controller is gone.

method.name: client_spawn_pawn
method.description: Remote call: build a pawn the server spawned, from the scene the server named. A pawn a script instantiated itself is never mirrored - this is why the game mode names pawn scenes rather than building them.

method.name: client_spawn_player_state
method.description: Remote call: build a player state the server created.

method.name: client_travel_to_level
method.description: Remote call: tells a client to load [param level_path]. It reports back with [method server_notify_level_loaded], and only then is handed the world as it stands.

method.name: get_ready_peers
method.description: Every peer with the current level built. Cleared whenever the level changes.

method.name: get_world
method.description: The world this driver belongs to.

method.name: is_peer_ready
method.description: Whether [param peer_id] has reported the current level built. Nothing is sent to a peer before that, which is what makes a late join and a level change the same case.

method.name: server_notify_level_loaded
method.description: Remote call: a client telling the server its level is built. The server then sends it everything it missed - player states first, then pawns, then its own controller.
